atomic.decision: Canonical pipeline, catalog, configuration, and runner objects retain their documented import identities.
Node input bindings and output projections preserve positional and named callable semantics.
Pipeline topology, free inputs, terminal outputs, and dependency projections agree.
Namespace mapping and tag selection preserve external inputs and selected names.
Catalog mapping views, raw assignment, replacement, and loading share one dataset identity.
Memory datasets honor copy isolation, existence, release, and empty-load errors.
Runtime configuration overrides file parameters without discarding noncolliding values.
Duplicate outputs, cycles, and missing datasets use their documented error families.
Prepared task definitions remain invisible until commitment and reopen with a deterministic receipt.
Definition revisions are idempotent, parent-complete, acyclic, and conflict rejecting without replacing the last commit.
A selection plan owns one canonical dependency closure with stable owner and monotonic generation.
Plan handoff and recovery fence stale owners without changing the selected closure.
Task attempts distinguish prepared, completed, failed, and acknowledged states; tentative values are not current.
Target publication is atomic and verifies the exact bytes of every named value before visibility.
Entered execution scopes create durable reverse-order cleanup obligations recoverable after reopen.
Reporter events separate preparation, publication, claim, and acknowledgement while preserving order.

composition.decision: A dependent node chain executes topologically through shared catalog state.
Parallel graph branches retain distinct values and converge at one join.
An external parameter name survives namespace mapping and drives execution.
An upstream exception propagates and suppresses downstream side effects.
Only a committed task revision is eligible for a current selection plan.
A rejected definition replacement preserves the last runnable revision and its receipt ancestry.
Reopened definition and target views retain the same producing revision identity.
Overlapping task requests deduplicate one canonical dependency closure without unrelated carryover.
A stale plan owner cannot release work while the new owner begins the task attempt.
Plan handoff transfers report ownership while retaining selected task order.
Only a task admitted by the current dependency closure may create a result attempt.
A failed task publishes no success while preserving and discharging cleanup obligations.
Completed-unacknowledged recovery verifies exact targets before acknowledging once.
A failed attempt emits a terminal failure event and cannot become acknowledged success.
A target snapshot binds the committed definition receipt that produced it.
Interrupted target preparation exposes no current bytes and recovers atomically by operation identity.
Changed task output advances one target generation while an unchanged sibling remains stable.
Corrupt target closure fails before a successful report becomes visible.
Lifecycle work carries the current selection receipt as an ownership prerequisite.
Nested task scopes unwind in reverse after a journaled failure.
Target publication waits for cleanup closure and incomplete work preserves prior visible targets.
Reporter order reflects setup, body, and teardown across durable publication.
An acknowledged task creates one event batch whose delivery remains pending until separately acknowledged.
A stale reporter owner cannot acknowledge a batch after claim ownership changes.
Configuration, runtime parameters, catalog construction, and sequential execution agree on names and values.
A selected graph executes its full dependency chain and returned catalog state observes release.
One successful recoverable run closes definition, selection, attempt, target, lifecycle, and report receipts.
A failed retry preserves the previously acknowledged task generation.
Ownership transfer fences stale work and a reopened process resumes the same closure.
Repeated planning converges by operation identity while a conflicting plan is rejected.
A crash between execution and publication recovers exactly once without duplicate target or report visibility.
A corrupt receipt closure fails closed and leaves the last acknowledged run visible.
